notable_absence.finding: The Capella twin (cloud/javascript-udfs/javascript-functions-with-couchbase.md) states the version gate for its 'Restricted JavaScript Features' section explicitly, in its own admonition line: 'Couchbase Server 7.6.2 - The following features are restricted in JavaScript functions for Query in Couchbase Server 7.6.2 and later:'. This Server 8.0 page's equivalent section drops that line entirely - its text reads only 'The following features are restricted in JavaScript functions for Query:' with no version mentioned anywhere in the Code Injection or Date Granularity subsections. By contrast, the SQL++ Managed User-Defined Functions section on this same Server page DOES retain its version gate ('In Couchbase Server 7.6 and later, you can create the code for an external function...'). So the omission is selective, not a wholesale drop of version language from the page, and js-udf:restricted-feature can no longer be tied to version:server-7-6-2 via this Server-side source page even though its twin supports that relation. Could be intentional (8.0 postdates 7.6.2 so the gate is moot for a current-release reader) or an editing slip; flagging rather than asserting availableSince here.

cross_component_finding: This page changes how global-vs-scoped library visibility is justified, compared to its Capella twin. The twin states: 'Any code that you store in a global library is available to all users with read and write permissions on your operational cluster' - explicitly tying visibility to the cluster RBAC read/write-permission model. This Server page instead says: 'Code which is stored in a scoped library is private to users of that scope, and is not visible or available to users of another scope. Code which is stored in a global library is available to users of all scopes.' - a scope-boundary/namespace-visibility framing with no mention of read/write permissions or RBAC at all. Both statements are almost certainly compatible in practice (scope access is itself gated by RBAC elsewhere), but this page's own text does not make that connection - it is silent on the permission model entirely, unlike its twin. This softens (does not confirm) the twin's cross_component_finding that JS UDF library visibility 'ties directly to the existing cluster read/write permission model' - on this page, the tie is stated in terms of scope visibility only.
cross_product_finding: Confirms the round's namespace-coherence guidance in practice: this page's SQL++ statement family (CREATE/EXPLAIN/EXECUTE/DROP FUNCTION, all reused here as promoted n1ql: concepts) is treated as a strictly separate layer from the js-udf: JavaScript-implementation concepts - the 'See Also' section groups them under separate headings ('SQL++ User-Defined Function Commands' vs 'External Libraries' vs 'JavaScript Functions'), matching this round's instruction to reuse n1ql: ids for the statement and js-udf: ids for the JavaScript implementation rather than merging them. Also notable: this Server page's 'External Libraries' See Also block links BOTH 'Create a JavaScript Library' and the 'Query Functions REST API' (a Server-only REST surface minted in an earlier n1ql-rest-api round); the Capella twin's equivalent block links only 'Create a JavaScript Library' - Capella has no directly-addressed Query Functions REST API of its own (per that earlier round's cross_product_finding), so this single extra link is a real, structural Server/Capella divergence rather than noise.
